aboutPageDescription: About NaMe Magazine — a platform for artists before the world knows their names
aboutBody:
NaMe Magazine is a platform for artists before the world knows their names. Rooted in the theme “Before the Name,” the magazine exists to support photographers, designers, filmmakers, writers, and visual artists whose voices are still forming outside of mainstream visibility.

Why NaMe exists

We believe that before recognition, awards, or industry validation, there is first the desire to create and to be seen. NaMe Magazine was created to hold space for that moment—the period before an artist becomes a “name,” yet is already making meaningful work.

What we build

Through open calls, features, editorials, interviews, and online discussion, NaMe Magazine aims to build a growing archive and community centered around new creative voices from different mediums and backgrounds.

All mediums are welcome.

Before the world knows your name, there is only the desire to be seen.

Want to share your work? Visit Submission or Community.

By using NaMe Magazine you agree to these terms. Content is for personal, non-commercial viewing unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Members may comment on posts in accordance with our community standards. NaMe may remove content at any time.

Last updated: March 2026.
privacyBody:
This policy explains what NaMe Magazine collects, why we use it, and the choices you have. NaMe Publishing operates the site from New York.

Last updated: September 29, 2026.

Who this covers

This policy applies to people who visit the site, subscribe to the newsletter, or create a member account. If you only read the magazine, we store a language preference in your browser and do not require an account.

Information we collect

Account. When you join, we collect your email address, a display name, and a password. You may also add a profile photo and a short signature. We record whether you choose to receive the newsletter.

Newsletter. If you subscribe from the newsletter page, we store the email address you enter. An account is not required.

What you post. Members can comment on stories, like comments and community posts, and share community posts with a title, caption, and image. Those posts show your display name, photo, and signature to other visitors.

Submissions. If you submit work for editorial review, we store the title, medium, description, and the files you upload, such as images, PDFs, or video. We also store the review status and any note from an editor.

Messages. If you email us, we use your name, email address, and message to reply.

How we use it

  • Create and secure your account, and keep you signed in
  • Show your public profile beside comments and community posts
  • Review submissions and publish work we select
  • Send newsletters you opt into
  • Reply to email you send us
  • Remember your language on this device

We do not sell personal information, and we do not use it for third-party advertising.

Who can see it

Your display name, profile photo, signature, comments, and community posts are visible on the public pages where they appear. Your email address is not displayed with those posts.

Submissions are visible to you and to NaMe editors until a piece is published. Editors can see the newsletter list so we can send the messages you asked for.

Where it is stored

Accounts, profiles, comments, community posts, submissions, newsletter addresses, and uploaded files are stored with Supabase, which hosts our database and files. Passwords are held by that sign-in service in hashed form. NaMe staff cannot see your password.

In your browser, the site saves your language choice and, while you are signed in, a snapshot of your display name, email, photo, and role. That lets pages load in your language and show you as signed in. It stays on your device until you log out or clear this site's data. We do not run advertising or analytics trackers.

How long we keep it

We keep account information while your account is open. Comments and community posts stay until you or an editor remove them. We keep submissions for editorial review and as a record of work we considered. Newsletter addresses stay until you unsubscribe or ask us to delete them. We keep email correspondence for as long as we need it to handle your request.

Your choices

  • Update your display name, photo, and signature from your profile
  • Delete comments and community posts you created
  • Email namemagazinenyc@gmail.com to unsubscribe, close your account, or ask us to remove a submission or other personal information
  • Clear this site's data in your browser to remove the language preference and signed-in snapshot

Children

NaMe is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. If you believe a child has given us personal information, email us and we will delete it.

Updates

If we change this policy, we will post the new version on this page and update the date above.
